g.title: PH1_QSP
g.text: Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1 — Quantitative Systems Pharmacology Map
AGXT/AGT deficiency · glyoxylate futile cycle · calcium-oxalate crystal nephropathy · systemic oxalosis
substrate-reduction RNAi (lumasiran, nedosiran) · pyridoxine · crystallisation inhibitors · dialysis · liver-kidney transplantation

g.title: cluster_loops

g.title: L1
g.text: With AGT gone, carbon circulates and LDH
⇒ silencing GO cuts Uox ~65% and RAISES glycolate;
silencing LDHA cuts Uox without raising glycolate

g.title: L2
g.text: nephron loss raises oxalate load PER nephron,
⇒ self-accelerating; the eGFR curve bends downward

g.title: L3
g.text: falling GFR ⇒ Pox rises hyperbolically ⇒ tissue
deposition ⇒ bone stores buffer Pox (masking severity,
blunting the RNAi plasma response) ⇒ release for
months–years once a transplant restores clearance
